keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The infobox gives no area. Ming Yuzhen successfully conquered Sichuan (1357); the page does not say Xia held Guizhou or Yunnan: Guizhou appears only in an 1475 rebellion and Yunnan was a target that Xia failed to take. The shape is the province of Sichuan with Chongqing for all years, the page offering no frontier.

region.text: Sichuan and Chongqing, the land of Ming Yuzhen's Longshu and Xia

ledger.note: 1360: Ming Yuzhen takes the title of king of Longshu in Sichuan, refusing Chen Youliang. The Ming Xia page gives both 1360 and 1362 for Ming Yuzhen's claim to the King of Longshu title (the infobox dates Xia to 1362); he had ruled Sichuan since 1357 in Xu Shouhui's name.
1362: Ming Yuzhen becomes emperor of the Great Xia at Chongqing. Infobox Established 1362; he became emperor of the Great Xia 'with its capital in' Chongqing.

union.text: Mianzhou (Mianyang) in northern Sichuan, taken by Fu Youde in May 1371

region.text: northern Sichuan around Mianzhou and the Yangtze approach to Chongqing

ledger.note: May 1371: the Ming army takes northern Sichuan. Fu Youde attacked from the north and in May took Wenzhou [sic] and then captured Mianzhou in a night battle; Tang He and Liao Yongzhong advanced up the Yangtze.
August 1371: Chongqing falls and Ming Sheng surrenders. Tang He and Liao Yongzhong reached Chongqing, where the fifteen-year-old emperor Ming Sheng and his mother surrendered.

notes: Written for ea-06-x from the Ming Xia page (infobox, 1357 conquest, 1371 campaign), with the Tianwan page for the 1357-1360 vassal years (recorded as vassal events in tianwan) and the Red Turban page for the umbrella war. Cliopatria has no row. Start year: the infobox says Established 1362, but the page also dates the Longshu kingship to 1360 and Sichuan was ruled by Ming Yuzhen from 1357; the dossier starts in 1360 (confidence 2) so that Sichuan is not left without a ruler between Tianwan's end and the Xia. Disagreements: the Ming Xia page names Wenzhou and Mianzhou for the May 1371 conquests (Mianzhou is modern Mianyang; Wenzhou is read as the Sichuan-Gansu border prefecture and is not mapped); the Red Turban page says the failed attack on Yunnan took place under Ming Yuzhen but gives no year. Counterparts needing dossiers: ming-dynasty (Cliopatria slug; the Ming dossier should list this state as a conquest of 1371), tianwan (this batch). Reviewer ea-06-x (2026-10-24): every Sichuan region now leaves out Kham ({"minus": [Sichuan (region), Kham]}), because the gazetteer Sichuan (region) reaches 97.4 E and took in 1,021 cells (about 258,000 km2) of the Kham highlands that the Yuan administered as the Tuogansi route (Tibet under Yuan rule page), not as Sichuan.
